verdict.rationale: Mercury's documented API surface is broad. It covers transactions (metadata, attachments, categories), statements, treasury, card issuance, limits and lifecycle, Accounts Receivable invoices and customers, ACH/check/wire/international payouts, internal transfers and webhooks/events. A CLI, MCP server and agent skills also drive these workflows. However, no first-party claim of UI parity is made. Some workflows remain dashboard-bound: API-queued disbursements need manual sign-off inside the Mercury dashboard, and approvals follow organization policies. Several UI features (AI bill reading/bill pay, accounting sync, reimbursements, user permission management) have no evidenced API equivalent. Missing for 10: explicit API/UI parity commitment, API approval/sign-off of gated payments, bill pay and accounting-sync endpoints, user/permission and reimbursement management via API, independent hands-on confirmation of parity.
